candidates.rationale: Nearest-archive rho 0.792 sits right at the reject boundary, and working memory documents this exact chassis as window-stable (21d/42d correlate 0.950) so a window tweak won't decorrelate it. Per the same rule, swap which price field anchors the range instead: $high -> $open in the TS_MAX bound.

Highest one-way turnover in the batch (0.246) and a 2013 sign flip both trace to the noisy 10-day TS_STD normalizer; memory flags this exact denominator as a correlation collision point requiring a window/measure change, not just a numerator swap. Lengthening 10->21 smooths the rank and cuts turnover.

Only near-flat year is 2003 (+0.0005), a value-cyclicality dip from pairing a slow quarterly numerator with a single noisy daily close; memory rules out swapping the $roe leg (roe/leverage/roa all collide here). Smoothing the price anchor with a 5-day mean reduces that day-level noise without touching either fundamental leg.

Shortest-but-one IC half-life in the batch (4.0 days) and turnover 0.215 both trace to the fast 5-day open-delta leg. Lengthening it to 21 days targets a slower horizon and also pushes further from the w=10 sibling (rho 0.798) than a smaller bump would.

Working memory names this exact pattern -- TS_MIN($low) combined with a return term -- a correlation trap where the low-term sometimes adds no signal, and it sits at rho 0.780 against a sibling in this same batch. Re-anchoring the floor to $close addresses the flagged weak component directly.

Lowest coverage in the batch (0.934) and the only nonzero complexity charge (0.100) both stem from sitting at 4/5 distinct fields. Collapsing the redundant $low into $close drops field count to 3/5 and removes the complexity penalty without touching the fundamental leg or windows.

2012 IC flips negative (-0.0018) amid otherwise-positive years, a regime problem sourced in the short-term return-reversal leg; the value leg (eps/close) is the stable half. Lengthening the return window from 10 to 21 days targets slower, less whipsaw-prone momentum and also de-overlaps the literal TS_MEAN($return,10) subtree shared with the 693246 sibling (rho 0.780).

Dividing by a cross-sectional rank is a structural flaw: CS_RANK(...) is guaranteed near zero for the least-liquid name every single day, so the 1e-8 guard doesn't prevent an outlier blowup there -- a likely contributor to the 2013 sign flip. The archive neighbor already proves raw TS_MEAN($dollar_volume,21) is the sound denominator choice for this shape.

Worst turnover (0.294) and shortest IC half-life (3.0 days) in the whole batch both come from the 5-day realized-vol leg, too small a sample to be stable day to day. Widening it to 21 keeps the fast/slow vol-ratio concept intact while smoothing the noisiest component.

Mutual rho 0.798 against the w=5 sibling sits right at the reject line, and memory records this roe x dollar_volume-rank chassis as saturated regardless of window or second-leg changes. Swapping the accounting dimension (avoiding leverage, which fails cheap_screen in this exact template, and roa, which correlates ~0.86 with roe) is the untried lever.

prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.


TASK: MUTATE. For each parent below, identify its single weakest component and
change ONLY that component.

A mutation is localized: the returned expression must be within
3 tree edits of its parent. Rewriting the idea is not a mutation
and will be rejected. Say which node you changed in `changed_node`, and put the
parent's id in `parent_ids`.

Read the diagnostics: a factor whose IC is positive in most years and negative in two has a regime problem, one with high turnover is paying costs it does not earn back, and one whose IC half-life is short is being asked to predict too far ahead. Change the component responsible for the specific weakness you name.

Keep mining this pairing across windows and field pairs.

Retry marginal bare rejects with a fresh fundamental multiplier instead of discarding them.
  8. Swapping the price field in an accepted shape does not decorrelate: $adj_close vs $close in a book_per_share ratio hit rho 1.000, and $close vs $open inside a TS_DELTA(...,5) spread leg hit 0.839. Vary the operator or window, not which of open/high/low/close/adj_close fills a slot.

COUNT-style and sign-style kernels need a fundamental rank on the other leg to clear screen, as already proven for $roa.
  10. CS_RANK(TS_STD($return,5)) and CS_ZSCORE(TS_MEAN($dollar_volume,21)) are now saturated as standalone fragments, each triggering an archive_subtree reject regardless of the paired leg. Don't reuse either verbatim even with a new partner.
  11. This round's accepts skewed heavily to price_volume niches (7 of 9); only one touched a fundamental (operating_margin, landing in slow/mixed/high). If broader fundamental/mixed niche coverage matters, prioritize fundamental-crossed proposals next round before price_volume slots fill further.
  12. MIN($return,0) (raw downside truncation, no fundamental) missed cheap_screen at |t| 0.99, right at the threshold. Unlike EPS downside truncation which is productive, truncating raw $return alone is unproven; pair with a fundamental rather than resubmitting bare.
